deep_dive.title: Machine learning-based diagnostic decision support for suspected anterior cruciate ligament tears in clinically evaluated athletes
deep_dive.abstract: Anterior cruciate ligament tears (ACLT) may be difficult to identify at the initial clinical encounter because acute symptoms can limit examination and access to diagnostic tools may be constrained. This study evaluated supervised machine-learning models for ACLT decision support using routinely available initial clinical data. Data from 196 athletes with suspected ACLT (146 confirmed ACLT; 50 symptomatic non-ACLT) were represented by seven manually annotated binary clinical predictors. Participants were stratified into training (n = 137) and independent held-out evaluation (n = 59) sets. Eight classifiers were optimized using nested cross-validation within the training set and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC). Classification used a training-derived F1-optimal threshold of 0.50. Optuna-tuned XGBoost achieved the highest ROC-AUC (0.962) and F1-score (94.25%); XGBoost, support vector machine, and k-nearest neighbors achieved the highest recall (93.18%). SHAP analysis of XGBoost identified joint effusion as the strongest contributor to model output. These findings indicate that supervised machine-learning models based exclusively on initial clinical variables may support ACLT assessment at first presentation. Prospective external validation is required before clinical implementation.

deep_dive.title: Sex-Equitable Machine Learning Prediction of Ankle Reinjury in Individuals with Chronic Ankle Instability: A 2-Year Prospective Cohort Study with Fairness Audit
deep_dive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic ankle instability (CAI) face a 2-year reinjury rate approaching 50%, but individualized prediction models that quantify which baseline impairments predict subsequent reinjury within an established CAI cohort remain scarce, and existing prediction models for ankle injury have not assessed sex-related fairness. The aim was to develop and internally validate sex-equitable machine learning (ML) models predicting 2-year ankle reinjury in individuals with CAI, identify the most influential baseline prognostic markers, and audit sex-stratified model performance. METHODS: One hundred physically active individuals (50 male, 50 female) with CAI (mean age 21.8 ± 2.3 years) were recruited from a university population between February 2017 and February 2018 and prospectively followed for 2 years; 96 (49 male, 47 female) with at least one follow-up response were retained for analysis (41 reinjury events, 43% reinjury rate). Fourteen baseline predictors spanning demographic, anthropometric, injury-history, patient-reported, biomechanical, postural-control, and functional-performance domains were collected. Six algorithms were trained with nested cross-validation: an unpenalized logistic regression baseline and five ML algorithms (Elastic Net, support vector machine, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM). Predictive contribution of each feature was quantified using Shapley additive explanations and partial-dependence plots. A pre-specified fairness audit compared single global and sex-specific Youden thresholds derived out-of-fold using the equalized-odds gap and disproportionate-impact ratio. RESULTS: All algorithms achieved area under the curve (AUC) values above 0.70; Elastic Net was selected as the primary model (AUC = 0.807, 95% CI 0.714-0.893; calibration slope = 1.015). Sex, arch height index, previous sprains, dorsiflexion range of motion, and Biodex Overall Stability Index consistently emerged as the most influential prognostic markers. Within-sex discrimination was comparable between males and females, but a single global threshold produced an equalized-odds gap of 0.384 that was reduced by 57% (to 0.164) through sex-specific thresholding without retraining the model. CONCLUSIONS: ML models with a fairness-audited threshold strategy predicted 2-year ankle reinjury in individuals with CAI, reducing the equalized-odds gap by 57%, though the disproportionate-impact ratio (0.683) remained below the 0.80 benchmark. External validation is required before clinical deployment.

deep_dive.title: Wearable Sensor‐Based Prediction of Knee Joint Moments in Competitive Rugby Players During Multidirectional Movements
deep_dive.abstract: ABSTRACT This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning framework using plantar‐pressure sensors to estimate knee moments during rugby‐specific movements. A total of 31 North American competitive rugby players were recruited to perform four common rugby movements on an infilled artificial turf surface in a motion capture laboratory. Synchronized data acquisition was performed for plantar pressure, motion capture, and ground reaction forces. Knee moments were calculated via inverse dynamics. Genetic Algorithm‐Deep Forest Regression (GA‐DFR) was used to select plantar‐pressure sensors and predict resultant moments within participant‐level nested cross‐validation. Four alternative models predicted the resultant using the same layouts and participant splits. Complementary deep forest regression (DFR) models predicted the three moment components using these layouts. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpreted held‐out predictions. Layouts contained 7–18 sensors. Pooled resultant R 2 was 0.795, with root mean square error of 0.0512 N·m/N. DFR performed better than linear regression and the convolutional neural network, with no significant differences from the deep neural network or long short‐term memory network. Pooled R 2 was 0.806, 0.662, and 0.675 for flexion‐extension, adduction‐abduction, and internal‐external rotation moments, respectively. Resultant temporal SHAP contributions exceeded their stance‐wide mean during 9%–55% of stance, peaking at 24%. Reduced plantar‐pressure inputs supported estimation of resultant and direction‐specific knee‐moment waveforms in unseen rugby players.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 膝关节力矩评估通常依赖实验室动作捕捉与测力台，难以在真实训练场景中普及。本研究招募31名竞技橄榄球运动员完成四种变向动作，同步采集足底压力、动作捕捉与地面反作用力，并以逆动力学计算膝关节力矩。作者提出遗传算法结合深度森林回归的可解释框架，用于筛选压力传感器并预测力矩，在受试者级嵌套交叉验证下与四种替代模型比较。结果表明可穿戴传感器配合可解释机器学习可有效估计关节负荷，为运动损伤风险监测提供实用工具。

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 田径投掷项目的成绩预测通常依赖教练经验与少量手工指标，难以充分利用动作过程信息。本文提出Throwing4框架，将投掷动作分解为多个阶段并进行姿态建模，从中提取与投掷距离相关的运动学特征用于预测。该工作把计算机视觉姿态估计与阶段感知建模结合，用于精英运动员的成绩评估。其意义在于为运动表现分析提供可自动化的技术路径，但摘要信息有限，具体实验与结果尚待补充。
